record.title: Latvia prohibits non-exempt passenger movement at Russian and Belarusian land borders in March 2020
record.scope: External-EU land/rail and local-border-traffic crossings; internal-EU private travel excluded
record.crossings: Latvia–Russia and Latvia–Belarus external-border road, rail and local crossings
record.direction: Both directions, with asymmetric return and departure exceptions
record.movement: Non-exempt passengers and passenger vehicles, including Latvian citizens seeking eastern departure
record.exceptions: Freight, Latvian citizen/resident return, diplomats and humanitarian/national-interest cases; outward foreign travel and additional later exemptions were permitted.
record.enforcement: Legal movement prohibition and contemporary LSM report of midnight implementation; no independent count of refusals.
record.consequences: Eastern private travel was restricted while private travel at EU borders had different rules.
record.relationship: Separate imposing authority and movement category from neighbouring-country restrictions. Reciprocal policies must not be added as extra border-wide days.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026
record.official_rationale: Contain COVID-19 during the declared emergency.
record.context: International passenger carrier services were separately suspended. This record isolates the external-land movement prohibition, not the Baltic internal-border travel bubble.
record.uncertainty: Final end of this external-frontier regime is unresolved. Consolidated law and the later FAQ show changing exceptions. The Baltic May opening and the end of the June emergency are not treated as reopening of Russia/Belarus borders. Removal of testing requirements in April 2022 alone does not settle the earlier purpose prohibition.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. No claim of a continuous nationwide operational closure.
